description: Master your creative process with a copywriting brief template on Mac. Use Lazur to organize research, draft faster, and keep your focus on the writing.
intro: A solid copywriting brief template is the foundation of every successful project. When you use a consistent structure on your Mac, you stop guessing where to put client notes and start writing sooner.
tldr: Use a standardized copywriting brief template to capture client goals, target audience, and key messages.
Store your templates in apps like Notion or Ulysses to keep research and drafting in one place.

blocks.text: Why you need a copywriting brief template

Many copywriters start with a blank page. This is a mistake. A blank page invites distraction and procrastination. A well-built copywriting brief template acts as a map. It tells you exactly what to write next. When you have the audience, the tone, and the goal defined, the actual writing flows much faster. You spend less time wondering if you are on the right track.

On a Mac, you can keep this template in a dedicated folder. Use an app like Notion or Ulysses. When a new project arrives, duplicate your template. It takes two seconds. Then, fill it out. If you find yourself typing the same questions to clients, add those to your template. Over time, your template becomes a repository of your best questions.
How to structure your copywriting brief template

items: Project Goal: What is the single most important thing this copy must achieve?
Target Audience: Who are we writing to? What is their current pain point?
Key Message: What is the one thing the reader should remember?
Tone of Voice: Should it be professional, casual, or urgent?
Deliverables: Is this a landing page, an email, or a series of social posts?
Deadlines: When is the first draft due?

blocks.text: Keep these sections at the top of your document. If you use Notion, use a callout block to highlight the project goal. This ensures it stays visible even as you scroll down to draft. If you use Word, use a header that stays visible in the navigation pane. Keeping your goal in sight prevents scope creep.

Research is where most copywriters lose time. You jump between tabs, copy links, and forget where you found a specific stat. With Lazur, you can hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. If you are reading a competitor site, ask Lazur to summarize the key points. Lazur will answer out loud while you keep typing in your document.
When researching, ask Lazur to point at the relevant section on a webpage. Use the guide capability to learn how to extract data effectively without losing your place in your draft.
blocks.title: Use Lazur to stay focused

blocks.text: Sometimes your brain works faster than your fingers. When you feel stuck, hold the fn key to dictate your thoughts directly into your copywriting brief template. Do not worry about grammar yet. Just get the ideas out. Once the text is on the screen, use your keyboard to polish the phrasing. This method works well for initial brainstorming sessions where speed is more important than perfection.

Check your dictation accuracy if you find yourself editing too much. You can use the [dictation accuracy checker](/tools/dictation-accuracy-checker) to see if you need to enunciate more clearly. Remember that Lazur keeps your dictation clean and formatted. It does not store your audio or use it for training models.

Copywriters often report that their day is fragmented by communication. Slack, email, and meetings break your flow. Research shows it takes 23 minutes to refocus after an interruption. If you get interrupted three times, you have lost over an hour of productive time. Protect your morning hours for writing. Use your copywriting brief template to outline your work before you open any communication apps.

If a client sends an urgent message, check it, but do not reply immediately. Batch your responses for the afternoon. This keeps your morning for the creative work that actually moves the needle. Your copywriting brief template helps here too. When you return to your desk, you can see exactly where you left off.

items: Not updating the brief as the project evolves.
Trying to write without a clear goal defined in the template.
Skipping the audience research phase to save time.
Letting communication apps stay open during deep work blocks.
Using a different format for every client.

blocks.text: Stick to one format. If you use a template, make sure it is accessible. If you work in a team, share the template so everyone is on the same page. This reduces the time spent on revision rounds later. A clear brief is the best defense against endless feedback loops.

faq.question: What should I include in a copywriting brief template?
faq.answer: Include the project goal, target audience, key message, tone of voice, deliverables, and deadlines. Keep it simple and easy to scan.

faq.question: Can Lazur fill out my copywriting brief template for me?
faq.answer: Lazur does not edit files or type for you automatically. You can use the dictate capability to speak your notes into the template, or ask Lazur to explain concepts while you type.

faq.question: How do I stop getting distracted while writing?
faq.answer: Batch your communication tasks, turn off notifications, and keep your copywriting brief template open to stay focused on the project requirements.

faq.question: Is my data safe when using Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only listens and looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut. Your content is never used to train AI models.
